definitions.name: Fixed-law source-minimal completion fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)=\{\mathcal M=(Q,H):QV=H\varepsilon,\ Q,H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\ Q_{ii}=1\ (i\in\mathsf S),\ H\text{ is monomial},\ \det(Q)\ne0,\ [Q^{-1}H]_{\mathsf O,:}=C,\ \det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\}\)

definitions.name: Assigned source
definitions.construction: For \(\mathcal M=(Q,H)\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\), set \(s_{\mathcal M}(i)=j\) exactly when \(H_{ij}\ne0\)

definitions.name: Hard-intervention equilibrium effect
definitions.construction: \(\theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=\partial\,\operatorname{Eq}_{\mathcal M}(V_y\mid\operatorname{do}(V_x=t))/\partial t=(Q^{-1})_{yx}/(Q^{-1})_{xx}\)

definitions.name: Deletion-rank-admissible sources
definitions.construction: \(J_x(C)=\{j\in\mathsf S:C_{xj}\ne0\text{ and }\operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\}\)

definitions.name: Deletion-rank equilibrium-effect frontier
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)=\{C_{yj}/C_{xj}:j\in J_x(C)\}\)

definitions.name: Shear-and-matching completion certificate
definitions.construction: Extend the rows of \(C\) to \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\) and set \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). For each \(j\in J_x(C)\), retain \(T_j=T_0\) if \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\); otherwise choose \(\ell\in\mathsf L\) with \((W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0\) and set \(T_j=(I_n+e_\ell e_x^\top)T_0\), \(W_j=T_j^{-1}\). Find a perfect matching of the nonzero pattern of \((W_j)_{-j,-x}\), augment it by \(j\mapsto x\), and let \(\Pi_j\) be its row-permutation matrix. With \(D_j=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_jW_j)\), return \(Q_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_jW_j\), \(H_j=D_j^{-1}\Pi_j\), and \(\mathcal M_j=(Q_j,H_j)\)

definitions.name: Separated common-order OICA class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)=\{\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda):X=C\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^p,\ C\in\mathbb R^{p\times n},\lambda_j=\operatorname{cum}_r(\varepsilon_j),\ d\ge1,\ q\ge1,\ r=2d+q,\ n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d},\text{ and the listed source, normalization, cumulant, tensor, moment, loading, and deletion-margin properties hold for the indices }p,n,r,d,q\}\)

definitions.name: Common-order tensor-pencil inverse
definitions.construction: For each \(w\in\{u,v,e_1,\ldots,e_p\}\), contract the last \(q\) modes of \(\mathcal T_r\) against \(u^{\otimes(q-1)}\otimes w\) and matricize the remaining \(2d\) modes as \(M_w=V_d\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_j(u^\top c_j)^{q-1}(w^\top c_j))V_d^\top\). Let \(U\) be an orthonormal basis for \(\operatorname{range}(M_u)\), set \(A_w=U^\top M_wU\) and \(G_w=A_wA_u^{-1}\), form the spectral projector \(P_j\) of \(G_v\), and set \(z_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}(G_{e_i}P_j)\). Return \(c_j=z_j/\lVert z_j\rVert_2\), oriented by \(u^\top c_j>0\), up to a common permutation

definitions.name: Explicit local inverse constants
definitions.construction: \(\eta=\kappa\sigma^{q+2}\), \(\chi=\sqrt n/\sigma\), \(h=2/\eta+2n\Lambda/\eta^2\), \(\epsilon_0=\min\{\eta/2,\sigma/(6\chi h)\}\), \(L_z=nh\{2\chi+6n\Lambda\chi^2/(\eta\sigma)\}\), and \(L_C=2\sqrt{np}L_z\)

definitions.name: Clipped empirical cumulant tensor
definitions.construction: Compute every nonconstant raw empirical moment through total degree \(r\) from \(\mathbf X_N\), clip each coordinate to \([-B_m,B_m]\), and substitute the clipped vector into the moment-cumulant partition polynomial to obtain \(\widehat{\mathcal T}_r\)

definitions.name: Separated tensor minimum-distance fit
definitions.construction: Let \((\widehat C,\widehat\lambda)\) be the lexicographically selected minimizer of \(\lVert\widehat{\mathcal T}_r-\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda'_j(c'_j)^{\otimes r}\rVert_F\) over normalized pairs \((C',\lambda')\) satisfying the numerical restrictions defining \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\)

definitions.name: Estimated deletion-rank set
definitions.construction: \(\widehat J_x=\{j\in\mathsf S:\widehat C_{xj}\ne0\text{ and }\operatorname{rank}(\widehat C_{-x,-j})=p-1\}\)

definitions.name: Finite-sample simultaneous confidence union
definitions.construction: If \(2\tau_N<\epsilon_0\) and \(b_N<\min\{a,\delta\}/2\), set \(\mathcal U_{xy}=\bigcup_{j\in\widehat J_x}[\widehat C_{yj}/\widehat C_{xj}-w_N,\widehat C_{yj}/\widehat C_{xj}+w_N]\); otherwise set \(\mathcal U_{xy}=[-a^{-1},a^{-1}]\)

definitions.name: Coupled heterogeneous-order recovery handle
definitions.construction: Start from the Hessians of the cumulant-generating function at several arguments and the third-through-\(K\)th empirical cumulant slices; recover order-specific rank-one spans, intersect or jointly diagonalize their lifted spaces, and align components across orders by their shared normalized directions before applying the deletion-rank map
inputs: a finite or data-selected order cap \(K\)

definitions.name: Observational-law structural completion
Source-minimal observational-law completion fiber
definitions.construction:
For \(P_X=\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)\), let \(\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) be the set of all observational-law completions \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\) such that: \(Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}_{ii}=1\) for \(1\le i\le m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\); \(H^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\) is monomial; \(\det(Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}})\ne0\); \(\det(Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}_{-x,-x})\ne0\); the coordinates of \(\xi^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\) are mutually independent, nondegenerate, and non-Gaussian; \(A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\) has no zero column and no two proportional columns; and
\[
 \mathcal L\bigl(A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\xi^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\bigr)=P_X.
\]
No spectral-radius or dynamical-stability restriction is imposed.

definitions.name: Assigned source in a law completion
definitions.construction: For \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) and \(i\in\mathsf O\), define \(s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}^{\mathrm{law}}(i)\) to be the unique \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\}\) such that \(H^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}_{ik}\ne0\).

definitions.name: Reference-aligned source in a law completion
definitions.construction:
For \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) and \(i\in\mathsf O\), define the aligned source \(\bar s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(i)\) to be the unique \(j\in\mathsf S\) such that
\[
 A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}_{:,s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}^{\mathrm{law}}(i)}
 \in\operatorname{span}(c_j).
\]

definitions.name: Observed hard-intervention response vector
definitions.construction:
For \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\), define its observed hard-intervention equilibrium response vector by
\[
 \rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M})
 =\left(
 \frac{\partial}{\partial t}\operatorname{Eq}_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}
 \bigl(V_i^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\mid\operatorname{do}(V_x^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=t)\bigr)
 \right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}
 \in\mathbb R^{p-1}.
\]

definitions.name: Deletion-rank response-vector frontier
definitions.construction:
Define the response-vector frontier
\[
 \mathcal V_x(C)
 =\left\{
 \left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}
 :j\in J_x(C)
 \right\}\subseteq\mathbb R^{p-1}.
\]

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal M=(Q,H)\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\), if \(j=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\), then \(C_{xj}\ne0\) and \(\theta_{y\leftarrow x}(\mathcal M)=C_{yj}/C_{xj}\)

statements.gap: LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 derives square-ICA compatible systems, while no located result states this ratio over an arbitrary-latent fixed-law completion fiber.
statements.consumer: It permits an analyst to compute each candidate equilibrium effect without estimating or enumerating a structural graph.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\), its assigned source satisfies \(s_{\mathcal M}(x)\in J_x(C)\)
statements.justification: Deletion rank is the observable obstruction that rules out source assignments incompatible with a legal intervention.
statements.gap: DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 uses graph-level edge ranks and children bases, not numerical row-and-column deletion ranks for a fixed law.
statements.consumer: It provides a falsifiable certificate that removes impossible effect values before any completion is constructed.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M=(Q,H)\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\), set \(j=s_{\mathcal M}(x)\), and let \(h=H_{xj}\ne0\). Define
\[
 T=Q^{-1}H,\qquad W=T^{-1}=H^{-1}Q.
\]
By the fixed-law condition, \(T_{\mathsf O,:}=C\). Since \(H\) is monomial and its entry in row \(x\), column \(j\) is \(h\), row \(j\) of \(H^{-1}\) has its unique nonzero entry \(h^{-1}\) in column \(x\). The unit structural diagonal consequently implies
\[
 W_{jx}=(H^{-1}Q)_{jx}=h^{-1}Q_{xx}=h^{-1}\ne0. \tag{3}
\]
The inverse-cofactor formula for \(W=T^{-1}\) now gives
\[
 W_{jx}=\frac{(-1)^{j+x}\det(T_{-x,-j})}{\det(T)}.
\]
Because both \(W_{jx}\) and \(\det(T)\) are nonzero, \(T_{-x,-j}\) is nonsingular. Its rows indexed by \(\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\) are precisely the \(p-1\) rows of \(C_{-x,-j}\); a subset of the rows of a nonsingular matrix is linearly independent. Hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1. \tag{4}
\]
Finally, as in the adjugate calculation for the intervention ratio,
\[
 C_{xj}=(Q^{-1})_{xx}h
 =\frac{\det(Q_{-x,-x})}{\det(Q)}h\ne0,
\]
using observational and postintervention solvability. Equations (4) and the last display are exactly the two membership conditions for \(j\in J_x(C)\).

statements.statement: For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) returns a completion \(\mathcal M_j\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\) with \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\). If \(C\) is rational, the returned \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) are rational.
statements.justification: This is the nontrivial converse: one latent-row shear and one perfect matching realize every admissible ratio without changing the observed law.
statements.gap: The matching construction of DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 concerns compatible graph families; LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 has square row permutations and no latent-row shear.
statements.consumer: It yields exact audit models demonstrating that an apparent effect ambiguity is structural rather than numerical.
statements.proof_tex:
Because \(C\) has row rank \(p\), its rows extend to a basis of \(\mathbb R^n\); choose such an extension \(T_0\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb R)\) with \((T_0)_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and put \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). We first record the elementary deletion criterion
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})<p-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 e_j^{\top}\in\operatorname{rowspan}(C_{-x,:})
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 (W_0)_{jx}=0\ \text{ and }\ (W_0)_{j\ell}=0\ \text{ for every }\ell\in\mathsf L. \tag{5}
\]
For the first equivalence, the \(p-1\) rows of \(C_{-x,:}\) are independent because they are a subset of the independent rows of \(C\). Their restrictions to the coordinates other than \(j\) are dependent exactly when a nonzero linear combination is supported only at coordinate \(j\); independence before restriction makes that combination a nonzero multiple of \(e_j^{\top}\). For the second equivalence, the identity \(W_0T_0=I_n\) gives the unique expansion
\[
 e_j^{\top}=\sum_{i=1}^n (W_0)_{ji}(T_0)_{i,:}.
\]
It belongs to the span of the observed rows other than \(x\) exactly when its coefficients on row \(x\) and on all latent rows vanish. This proves (5).

Now fix \(j\in J_x(C)\). If \((W_0)_{jx}\ne0\), set \(T=T_0\) and \(W=W_0\). If \((W_0)_{jx}=0\), the full deletion rank in the definition of \(J_x(C)\), together with (5), supplies \(\ell\in\mathsf L\) with \((W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0\). Define
\[
 T=(I_n+e_\ell e_x^{\top})T_0,
 \qquad
 W=W_0(I_n-e_\ell e_x^{\top}). \tag{6}
\]
Since \(x\ne\ell\), \((e_\ell e_x^{\top})^2=0\), so the two shear matrices in (6) are inverse and \(W=T^{-1}\). The shear changes only latent row \(\ell\), hence \(T_{\mathsf O,:}=C\), and
\[
 W_{jx}=(W_0)_{jx}-(W_0)_{j\ell}=-(W_0)_{j\ell}\ne0. \tag{7}
\]
When \(n=p\), the set \(\mathsf L\) is empty and (5) shows directly that the second case cannot occur.

Since \(W^{-1}=T\) and \(T_{xj}=C_{xj}\ne0\), the cofactor identity gives
\[
 (-1)^{j+x}\det(W_{-j,-x})
 =\operatorname{cof}(W)_{jx}
 =\det(W)(W^{-1})_{xj}
 =\det(W)C_{xj}\ne0. \tag{8}
\]
Thus \(W_{-j,-x}\) is nonsingular. In the determinant expansion of this matrix, at least one permutation term is nonzero. Its nonzero entries give a perfect matching between the rows other than \(j\) and the columns other than \(x\). Augment that matching by assigning row \(j\) to column \(x\), and let \(\Pi\) be the row-permutation matrix placing every matched row in its matched column. All diagonal entries of \(\Pi W\) are nonzero. Therefore
\[
 D=\operatorname{diag}(\Pi W),\qquad
 Q=D^{-1}\Pi W,\qquad
 H=D^{-1}\Pi \tag{9}
\]
are well defined. The matrix \(H\) is monomial, \(Q\) is invertible, and (9) gives \(Q_{ii}=1\) for all \(i\). Moreover,
\[
 Q^{-1}H
 =W^{-1}\Pi^{-1}D D^{-1}\Pi
 =T,
\]
so \([Q^{-1}H]_{\mathsf O,:}=T_{\mathsf O,:}=C\). Row \(x\) of \(H\) has its unique nonzero entry in column \(j\), whence \(s_{\mathcal M_j}(x)=j\). Finally, deleting row and column \(x\) in (9) gives, up to the complementary row permutation,
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}=D_{-x,-x}^{-1}(\Pi W)_{-x,-x},
\]
and \((\Pi W)_{-x,-x}\) is a row permutation of the nonsingular matrix \(W_{-j,-x}\) from (8). Hence \(\det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\). All defining conditions of \(\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\) have now been verified.

If \(C\) is rational, Gaussian elimination can extend its rows using rational coordinate rows, so \(T_0\), \(W_0\), and the shear in (6) are rational. The permutation is integral, every entry of \(D\) is a nonzero rational number, and (9) uses only rational arithmetic and division by those entries. Thus the returned \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) are rational.

statements.statement:
Let \(P_X=\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)\). Under the population full-row-rank, nonzero distinct-direction, and independent nondegenerate non-Gaussian source assumptions, \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\), every \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) has \(m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=n\), and the sharp law-fiber response-vector set is
\[
 \left\{\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M}):\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\right\}
 =\mathcal V_x(C)
 =\left\{\left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}:C_{xj}\ne0,\ \operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\right\}.
\]
For every ordered \(y\ne x\), its scalar coordinate projection is exactly
\[
 \left\{[\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M})]_y:\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\right\}
 =\mathcal R_{xy}(C).
\]
The entire response vector is identified if and only if \(\mathcal V_x(C)\) is a singleton, and the \(y\)-coordinate effect is identified if and only if \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) is a singleton. If the latter is not a singleton, two indices with distinct ratios yield two exact same-law SCM countermodels via the canonical embeddings \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\) of the unchanged certificate construction. The frontiers are invariant under column permutation and nonzero rescaling, and all values together with one exact witness per value are certifiable in \(O(n^4)\) arithmetic operations. No stability assumption is imposed.
statements.justification: The theorem maps the entire source-minimal observational-law fiber to an exact finite response-vector frontier, with the original ordered effects as coordinate projections.
statements.gap: DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 supplies irreducible OICA direction recovery and graph-family equivalence, while TramontanoDrtonEtesami2026 studies coefficients conditional on a known mixed graph; neither derives the numerical intervention-response image of every completion of one observed law.
statements.consumer: For the fourteen-stock Hong Kong example of DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026, the population result replaces graph enumeration by at most one source-ratio response vector per recovered direction and supplies exact countermodels whenever a selected ordered stock effect is not identified.
statements.proof_tex:
The proof separates the causal target, which is the equilibrium response over the observational-law fiber, from the rank-and-ratio functional computed from a mixing representative.

First, \(J_x(C)\) is nonempty. The full-row-rank assumption permits extending the \(p\) rows of \(C\) to the invertible matrix \(T_0\) in the unchanged certificate definition; write \(W_0=T_0^{-1}\). The \((x,x)\) entry of \(T_0W_0=I_n\) is
\[
 1=\sum_{j=1}^n C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}. \tag{14}
\]
Thus some \(j\) has \(C_{xj}(W_0)_{jx}\ne0\). The inverse-cofactor identity gives
\[
 (W_0)_{jx}=(-1)^{x+j}\frac{\det((T_0)_{-x,-j})}{\det(T_0)}, \tag{15}
\]
so \((T_0)_{-x,-j}\) is nonsingular. Its observed rows other than \(x\), restricted away from column \(j\), are precisely the rows of \(C_{-x,-j}\). Every row subset of a nonsingular square matrix is linearly independent; hence \(\operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\). Together with \(C_{xj}\ne0\), the definition of \(J_x(C)\) proves nonemptiness.

For necessity, take any \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\). The law-fiber response-rank lemma, whose OICA step uses the exact Appendix B.1 uniqueness result and whose algebraic step canonicalizes the monomial disturbance matrix without changing \(Q\), gives
\[
 m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=n,
 \qquad
 j=\bar s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(x)\in J_x(C),
 \qquad
 \rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M})
 =\left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}. \tag{16}
\]
Thus every causal response in the law fiber belongs to \(\mathcal V_x(C)\).

For sufficiency, take a vector \(v\in\mathcal V_x(C)\). By the response-frontier definition there is \(j\in J_x(C)\) with
\[
 v=\left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}. \tag{17}
\]
The canonical exact-witness lemma invokes the unchanged shear-and-matching construction and embeds its output as \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon)\). It proves that this is a member of \(\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) and that its response vector is the right-hand side of (17). Hence every vector in \(\mathcal V_x(C)\) is attained. Combining this with (16) proves the sharp vector-set equality.

Projection onto coordinate \(y\) maps the vector indexed by \(j\) to \(C_{yj}/C_{xj}\). Applying this projection to both sides of the vector equality and invoking the definition of \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) proves the scalar equality. The frontier monomial-invariance lemma proves that these sets do not depend on the permutation or nonzero scaling chosen for the ICA columns, so the displayed rank-and-ratio sets are functionals of \(P_X\) on the stated law class rather than artifacts of one representative.

A target is identified over a model fiber exactly when it is constant on that fiber. The two sharp equalities therefore imply that the full response is identified exactly when \(\mathcal V_x(C)\) has one element, and its \(y\)-coordinate is identified exactly when \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) has one element. If \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) is not a singleton, choose \(j,k\in J_x(C)\) with
\[
 \frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}\ne\frac{C_{yk}}{C_{xk}}. \tag{18}
\]
The two canonical embeddings \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j\) and \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_k\) both have observed law \(P_X\), satisfy observational and postintervention solvability, and have different \(y\)-coordinate responses by (18). They are the promised exact SCM countermodels.

Finally, Gaussian elimination extends \(C\) to \(T_0\) and computes \(W_0\) in \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic operations. For each of at most \(n\) columns, computing the rank of the \((p-1)\)-by-\((n-1)\) deletion matrix costs \(O(n^3)\), so all membership decisions for \(J_x(C)\) cost \(O(n^4)\). For each admissible index, the unchanged certificate uses one \(O(n^2)\) shear, one perfect matching in an \((n-1)\)-by-\((n-1)\) nonzero pattern computable by an augmenting-path method in \(O(n^3)\), and \(O(n^2)\) row normalization. Across at most \(n\) witnesses this is \(O(n^4)\). Forming all response ratios and discarding duplicate vectors or scalar values costs at most \(O(n^2)\) additional arithmetic comparisons. Therefore the overall certificate cost is \(O(n^4)\). Exact zero tests and arithmetic are meant in the real-arithmetic model; when \(C\) is rational, the canonical-witness lemma supplies rational \(Q_j,H_j\). No step invokes a stability restriction. Moment determinacy is not used in this population argument.

statements.statement:
Let \(P_X=\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)\). Suppose that \(\operatorname{rank}(C)=p\), every column of \(C\) is nonzero, no two columns of \(C\) are proportional, and the coordinates of \(\varepsilon\) are mutually independent, nondegenerate, and non-Gaussian. The law-fiber response vector \(\rho_x\) is point identified over \(\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) if and only if \(|\mathcal V_x(C)|=1\), equivalently \(|J_x(C)|=1\). If this vector criterion fails, there are distinct \(j,k\in J_x(C)\) for which the canonical embeddings of the completions returned by \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\) are two exact same-observational-law members \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j,\widetilde{\mathcal M}_k\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\), both satisfying postintervention solvability, such that \(\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j)\ne\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_k)\). They can be constructed in \(O(n^3)\) additional arithmetic operations after the shared basis extension and inverse. For every \(y\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\), the scalar coordinate \([\rho_x]_y\) is point identified over the same law fiber if and only if
\[
 |\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1,
 \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
 \operatorname{rank}\!\left(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)}\right)=1.
\]
If this scalar criterion fails, two canonical witnesses have distinct \(y\)-coordinate responses. Each scalar frontier is the corresponding coordinate projection of \(\mathcal V_x(C)\); the claim does not combine coordinates arising from different source indices into a response vector.
statements.justification: Separate vector and scalar singleton tests make the distinction between joint response identification and coordinatewise identification operational.
statements.gap: No cited cyclic latent result gives the law-fiber criterion \(|J_x(C)|=1\) for the whole response vector or the two exact same-law witness certificate.
statements.consumer: A user receives one coherent response vector or two complete structural models demonstrating ambiguity, while scalar effects remain valid coordinate projections.
statements.proof_tex:
Point identification of the entire response vector means that the map
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal M}\longmapsto\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M}),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X),
\]
is constant. By the sharp-effect-frontier theorem, its image is the nonempty set
\[
 \mathcal V_x(C)
 =\left\{\phi_x(j):j\in J_x(C)\right\},
 \qquad
 \phi_x(j)=\left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}. \tag{1}
\]
Thus the response vector is point identified if and only if \(|\mathcal V_x(C)|=1\). It remains to express this test directly in terms of \(J_x(C)\).

For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), the definition of \(J_x(C)\) gives \(C_{xj}\ne0\), so every division in (1) is valid. Suppose \(j,k\in J_x(C)\) and \(\phi_x(j)=\phi_x(k)\). Coordinatewise equality in (1) gives
\[
 \frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}=\frac{C_{ik}}{C_{xk}}
 \quad\text{for every }i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}. \tag{2}
\]
At coordinate \(x\), both normalized columns have value one. Adjoining this coordinate to (2) yields
\[
 \frac{c_j}{C_{xj}}=\frac{c_k}{C_{xk}},
 \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
 c_j=\frac{C_{xj}}{C_{xk}}c_k. \tag{3}
\]
The scalar in (3) is nonzero because both denominators and numerators are nonzero. Equation (3) says that \(c_j\) and \(c_k\) are proportional. The pairwise nonproportionality assumption therefore forces \(j=k\). Hence \(\phi_x\) is injective on the finite set \(J_x(C)\), and (1) implies
\[
 |\mathcal V_x(C)|=|J_x(C)|. \tag{4}
\]
Because the sharp-effect-frontier theorem also gives \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\), equations (1)--(4) prove the claimed vector criterion.

If that criterion fails, nonemptiness and (4) give distinct \(j,k\in J_x(C)\) with \(\phi_x(j)\ne\phi_x(k)\). The canonical-exact-law-witness lemma applies separately to these two indices. It gives canonical embeddings
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal M}_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon),
 \qquad
 \widetilde{\mathcal M}_k=(n,Q_k,H_k,\varepsilon)
\]
in \(\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) and gives
\[
 \rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j)=\phi_x(j)\ne
 \phi_x(k)=\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_k). \tag{5}
\]
Membership in \(\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\), by the definition of that fiber, proves separately that each system has observational law \(P_X\), that its structural matrix is invertible, and that its postintervention minor at \(x\) is invertible. Thus (5) supplies two exact same-observational-law, postintervention-solvable SCM countermodels; no stability restriction has been invoked.

We next prove the scalar corollary without replacing the jointly attainable vector set by a Cartesian product. The scalar part of the sharp-effect-frontier theorem gives
\[
 \left\{[\rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M})]_y:
 \widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\right\}
 =\mathcal R_{xy}(C)
 =\left\{\frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}:j\in J_x(C)\right\}. \tag{6}
\]
Consequently the \(y\)-coordinate is point identified if and only if \(|\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1\). Consider the two-row matrix \(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)}\). Since \(J_x(C)\ne\varnothing\) and \(C_{xj}\ne0\) for every \(j\in J_x(C)\), its \(x\)-row is nonzero and its rank is at least one. Its rank is at most one if and only if all its two-column minors vanish, namely if and only if
\[
 C_{xj}C_{yk}-C_{xk}C_{yj}=0
 \quad\text{for every }j,k\in J_x(C). \tag{7}
\]
For every such pair, division of (7) by the nonzero product \(C_{xj}C_{xk}\) is legitimate and gives
\[
 \frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}=\frac{C_{yk}}{C_{xk}}. \tag{8}
\]
Thus (7) is equivalent to all elements of the nonempty set in (6) being equal. Combining the rank lower bound with (7)--(8) proves
\[
 |\mathcal R_{xy}(C)|=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{rank}\!\left(C_{\{x,y\},J_x(C)}\right)=1. \tag{9}
\]
If (9) fails, (7) fails for some \(j,k\in J_x(C)\), so their ratios in (8) differ. Applying the canonical-exact-law-witness lemma to this pair gives two systems whose \(y\)-coordinate responses differ. Equation (1), however, shows that every whole response vector uses one common source index \(j\); equations (6)--(9) only take coordinate projections and never authorize cross-index recombination.

Finally, the witness algorithm shares one row-basis extension and one \(n\)-by-\(n\) matrix inverse. After those shared operations, each selected index requires at most one rank-one row shear, one perfect matching in an \((n-1)\)-by-\((n-1)\) nonzero pattern, and row permutation and normalization. A direct augmenting-path implementation performs at most \(n-1\) augmentations, each examining \(O(n^2)\) incidences, so one matching costs \(O(n^3)\) arithmetic and zero-test operations; the shear and normalization cost \(O(n^2)\). Repeating this for two fixed indices remains \(O(n^3)\), which proves the stated additional-operation bound.

statements.statement: When \(n=p\), the latent-row shear is unnecessary. Section 4 of LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 constructs candidate models from admissible row permutations, and its Theorem 1 states that the output of LiNG-D is a distribution-entailment equivalence class. Among those square admissible row-permutation candidates, restrict to the candidates satisfying \(\det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\). The projection of this postintervention-solvable subset onto \(\theta_{y\leftarrow x}\) equals \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\).
statements.justification: The square reduction transfers the exact frontier to precisely those foundational row-permutation candidates on which the hard-intervention equilibrium is defined.
statements.gap: LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 gives candidate construction and distribution entailment, but does not filter a specified intervention minor or identify its effect projection.
statements.consumer: Square cyclic-LiNG analyses can compute the query frontier after discarding candidates with singular postintervention systems.

statements.statement: For two members of \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\) with cumulant tensors \(\mathcal T_r\) and \(\mathcal T'_r\), if \(\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F<\epsilon_0\), then a permutation \(\pi\) exists such that \(\lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F\le L_C\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F\). The map \(\operatorname{OICAInv}\) recovers the directions attaining this bound.
statements.justification: An explicit inverse modulus is the bridge from moment uncertainty to uncertainty for a discontinuously selected causal set.
statements.gap: WangSeigal2026 gives population OICA identifiability and coupled recovery, while AnandkumarGeJanzamin2015 gives component perturbation bounds; neither supplies this local inverse for deletion-rank effect inference.
statements.consumer: It supplies the numerical certificate needed to distinguish real effect ambiguity from instability of tensor decomposition.
statements.proof_tex:
All unlabeled matrix norms below are operator two-norms. Let \(\Delta=\lVert\mathcal T'_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F<\epsilon_0\). For each probe \(w\in\{u,v,e_1,\ldots,e_p\}\), contraction against unit vectors and orthogonal compression have norm at most one. Consequently, if \(M_w,M'_w\) are the contracted matricizations, then
\[
 \lVert M'_w-M_w\rVert\le\Delta.
\]

Choose an orthonormal basis \(U\) for \(\operatorname{range}(V_d)\), set \(S=U^{\mathsf T}V_d\), and compress both tensors into this same space:
\[
 A_w=U^{\mathsf T}M_wU,
 \qquad A'_w=U^{\mathsf T}M'_wU.
\]
The lifted-rank margin makes \(S\) invertible, with
\[
 s_{\min}(S)=s_{\min}(V_d)\ge\sigma,
 \qquad \lVert S\rVert\le\lVert V_d\rVert_F=\sqrt n,
 \qquad \operatorname{cond}(S)\le\chi=\frac{\sqrt n}{\sigma}.
\]
Writing
\[
 D_w=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\lambda_j(u^{\mathsf T}c_j)^{q-1}(w^{\mathsf T}c_j)\right),
\]
the tensor factorization gives \(A_w=SD_wS^{\mathsf T}\). In particular, the cumulant and orientation margins imply
\[
 s_{\min}(A_u)
 \ge s_{\min}(S)^2\min_j|\lambda_j(u^{\mathsf T}c_j)^q|
 \ge\kappa\sigma^{q+2}=\eta,
\]
whereas unit columns and \(|\lambda_j|\le\Lambda\) imply
\[
 \lVert A_w\rVert\le \lVert V_d\rVert^2\Lambda\le n\Lambda.
\]
Since \(\Delta<\eta/2\), the elementary Neumann identity
\[
 A'_u=A_u\{I+A_u^{-1}(A'_u-A_u)\}
\]
shows that \(A'_u\) is invertible and \(\lVert(A'_u)^{-1}\rVert\le2/\eta\). The primed exact factorization is
\[
 A'_u=S'D'_u(S')^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad S'=U^{\mathsf T}V'_d.
\]
Every diagonal entry of \(D'_u\) is nonzero; invertibility of \(A'_u\) therefore forces the square matrix \(S'\) to be invertible.

Define \(G_w=A_wA_u^{-1}\) and \(G'_w=A'_w(A'_u)^{-1}\). The inverse identity and the preceding bounds give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert G'_w-G_w\rVert
 &\le \lVert A'_w-A_w\rVert\lVert(A'_u)^{-1}\rVert
   +\lVert A_w\rVert\lVert(A'_u)^{-1}(A_u-A'_u)A_u^{-1}\rVert\\
 &\le\left(\frac2\eta+\frac{2n\Lambda}{\eta^2}\right)\Delta
 =h\Delta.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Exact cancellation of the diagonal factors yields
\[
 G_w=S\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{w^{\mathsf T}c_j}{u^{\mathsf T}c_j}\right)S^{-1},
 \qquad
 G'_w=S'\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{w^{\mathsf T}c'_j}{u^{\mathsf T}c'_j}\right)(S')^{-1}.
\]

We next pair the two spectra without presupposing a label. Let \(\rho_j=v^{\mathsf T}c_j/(u^{\mathsf T}c_j)\), let \(g=\sigma/3\), and let \(\Gamma_j\) be the positively oriented complex circle of radius \(g\) about \(\rho_j\). The gap assumption makes these circles disjoint. For \(z\in\Gamma_j\), diagonalization gives
\[
 \lVert(zI-G_v)^{-1}\rVert\le\frac{\chi}{g}.
\]
For \(G_v(t)=G_v+t(G'_v-G_v)\), \(0\le t\le1\), the condition \(\Delta<\sigma/(6\chi h)\) gives
\[
 \lVert t(G'_v-G_v)(zI-G_v)^{-1}\rVert
 \le \frac{\chi h\Delta}{g}<\frac12.
\]
Thus the Neumann series makes every \(zI-G_v(t)\) invertible and bounds its inverse by \(2\chi/g\). Define entrywise
\[
 P_j(t)=\frac{1}{2\pi\mathrm i}\int_{\Gamma_j}(zI-G_v(t))^{-1}\,dz.
\]
At \(t=0\), direct integration of the displayed diagonalization gives \(P_j(0)=SE_{jj}S^{-1}\), a rank-one projector. The resolvent identity verifies directly that every \(P_j(t)\) is idempotent; it is continuous in \(t\), so its trace, equal to its integer rank, is constantly one. At \(t=1\) the \(n\) disjoint rank-one projectors account for all \(n\) eigenvalues and hence define a permutation pairing of the primed and unprimed components. Relabel the primed components by this permutation and write \(P'_j=P_j(1)\).

The resolvent identity under the same contour bounds yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lVert P'_j-P_j\rVert
 &\le \frac{1}{2\pi}(2\pi g)
 \frac{\chi}{g}\,h\Delta\,\frac{2\chi}{g}
 =\frac{6\chi^2h}{\sigma}\Delta,\\
 \lVert P_j\rVert&\le\chi,
 \qquad
 \lVert P'_j\rVert\le\lVert P_j\rVert+\lVert P'_j-P_j\rVert<2\chi.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For each coordinate probe, simultaneous diagonalization and cyclicity of trace give
\[
 z_{ij}:=\operatorname{tr}(G_{e_i}P_j)=\frac{c_{ij}}{u^{\mathsf T}c_j},
 \qquad
 z'_{ij}:=\operatorname{tr}(G'_{e_i}P'_j)=\frac{c'_{ij}}{u^{\mathsf T}c'_j}.
\]
Since \(|\operatorname{tr}K|\le n\lVert K\rVert\) and \(\lVert G_{e_i}\rVert\le n\Lambda/\eta\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |z'_{ij}-z_{ij}|
 &\le n\lVert G'_{e_i}-G_{e_i}\rVert\lVert P'_j\rVert
 +n\lVert G_{e_i}\rVert\lVert P'_j-P_j\rVert\\
 &\le nh\left(2\chi+\frac{6n\Lambda\chi^2}{\eta\sigma}\right)\Delta
 =L_z\Delta.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The orientation and unit-normalization conditions give
\[
 \lVert z_j\rVert_2=(u^{\mathsf T}c_j)^{-1}\ge1,
 \qquad
 \lVert z'_j\rVert_2=(u^{\mathsf T}c'_j)^{-1}\ge1,
\]
and \(c_j=z_j/\lVert z_j\rVert_2\), with the same formula for \(c'_j\). For nonzero vectors of norm at least one, adding and subtracting the common denominator shows
\[
 \left\lVert\frac{z'}{\lVert z'\rVert_2}-\frac{z}{\lVert z\rVert_2}\right\rVert_2
 \le2\lVert z'-z\rVert_2.
\]
Hence each paired column obeys \(\lVert c'_j-c_j\rVert_2\le2\sqrt p L_z\Delta\), and summing squared column bounds gives
\[
 \lVert C'_{\pi}-C\rVert_F
 \le2\sqrt{np}L_z\Delta=L_C\Delta.
\]
The projector-trace formulas are exactly the declared map \(\operatorname{OICAInv}\); applying them with each tensor's own range basis changes only the diagonalizing coordinates and returns the same normalized directions. Thus that map recovers the directions attaining the bound.

statements.statement: For every \(N\) and every nonempty class \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\) with \(d\ge1\), \(q\ge1\), and \(n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d}\), the iid confidence unions satisfy \[\inf_{\zeta=(P_X,C,\varepsilon,\lambda)\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}}P_X^{\otimes N}\!\left\{\begin{array}{l}\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\subseteq\mathcal U_{xy}\text{ for every }x\ne y\in\mathsf O,\\ \text{and, if }2\tau_N<\epsilon_0\text{ and }b_N<\min\{a,\delta\}/2,\text{ then after one common permutation}\\ \widehat J_x=J_x(C)\text{ and }d_H(\mathcal U_{xy},\mathcal R_{xy}(C))\le2w_N\text{ for every }x\ne y\in\mathsf O\end{array}\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Uniformly over the same representation-indexed tuples in the informative regime, \(2w_N=O(N^{-1/2})\).
statements.justification: The theorem makes the finite causal frontier inferentially usable and measures uncertainty by Hausdorff error rather than by the nonshrinking diameter of a genuinely multivalued set.
statements.gap: Existing OICA papers recover directions or bound component error, but no located paper gives simultaneous uniform coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff uncertainty for a rank-selected finite causal frontier.
statements.consumer: It supports honest iid uncertainty reports for laboratory or cross-sectional latent systems whose source directions satisfy an empirical separation certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a tuple \(\zeta\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\). Unit normalization gives
\[
 \lVert X\rVert_2\le\sum_{j=1}^n|\varepsilon_j|.
\]
The convexity inequality \((\sum_j t_j)^{2r}\le n^{2r-1}\sum_jt_j^{2r}\), followed by the source-moment envelope, yields
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert X\rVert_2^{2r}
 \le n^{2r-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\mathbb E|\varepsilon_j|^{2r}
 \le n^{2r}M\le H. \tag{13}
\]
Let \(\mu\in\mathbb R^m\) collect the nonconstant raw moments through total degree \(r\), and let \(\widetilde\mu\) be their untrimmed empirical averages. If a coordinate has degree \(k\le r\), its squared monomial is bounded by \(1+\lVert X\rVert_2^{2r}\). Thus (13) gives variance at most \(1+H\) for every coordinate and
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert\widetilde\mu-\mu\rVert_2^2
 \le\frac{m(1+H)}{N}. \tag{14}
\]
Moreover every true coordinate has absolute value at most \((1+H)^{1/2}\le B_m\). Coordinatewise clipping to \([-B_m,B_m]\) is projection onto an interval containing the true coordinate, so it cannot increase the Euclidean error. Markov's inequality applied to (14) therefore proves, for
\[
 E_N=\{\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert_2\le e_N\},
\qquad
 \inf_{\zeta\in\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}}P_X^{\otimes N}(E_N)\ge1-\alpha. \tag{15}
\]

For an ordered tensor coordinate, the moment--cumulant formula is
\[
 \operatorname{cum}(X_{i_1},\ldots,X_{i_r})
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_r}(-1)^{|\pi|-1}(|\pi|-1)!
   \prod_{A\in\pi}\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{k\in A}X_{i_k}\right]. \tag{16}
\]
On the moment box \([-B_m,B_m]^m\), telescoping a product with \(|\pi|\) factors bounds its change by \(|\pi|B_m^{|\pi|-1}\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert_2\). There are \(p^r\) ordered tensor coordinates, so (16) and the Frobenius norm give, on \(E_N\),
\[
 \lVert\widehat{\mathcal T}_r-\mathcal T_r\rVert_F
 \le p^{r/2}\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_r}(|\pi|-1)!|\pi|B_m^{|\pi|-1}e_N
 =\tau_N. \tag{17}
\]

The true normalized factor pair is feasible for the minimum-distance problem. The feasible numerical restrictions are closed and bounded: the columns lie on unit spheres, the cumulants lie in the compact set \(\{t:\kappa\le|t|\le\Lambda\}\), and all singular-value, loading, and pencil-gap restrictions are closed. Nonemptiness is assumed. Hence a minimizer exists, and the fixed lexicographic selection makes \((\widehat C,\widehat\lambda)\) a statistic. Its optimality and (17) imply
\[
 \left\lVert\sum_j\widehat\lambda_j\widehat c_j^{\otimes r}
       -\mathcal T_r\right\rVert_F
 \le 2\tau_N. \tag{18}
\]
The deterministic tensor-pencil argument in the common-order local-inverse lemma uses only the numerical restrictions imposed on these two factor pairs. Therefore, if \(2\tau_N<\epsilon_0\), (18) supplies one common permutation under which
\[
 \lVert\widehat C-C\rVert_F\le 2L_C\tau_N=b_N. \tag{19}
\]

Suppose also \(b_N<\min\{a,\delta\}/2\). Both \(C\) and the feasible fit obey the alternative that each loading is zero or has magnitude at least \(a\). Hence (19) prevents a zero loading in either matrix from being paired with a nonzero loading in the other. The zero patterns agree. For every deletion matrix, Weyl's singular-value inequality and (19) give
\[
 \left|s_{\min}(\widehat C_{-i,-j})-s_{\min}(C_{-i,-j})\right|
 \le\lVert\widehat C-C\rVert_F<\delta/2.
\]
Because each of the two feasible singular values is either zero or at least \(\delta\), their zero status agrees. Consequently \(\widehat J_x=J_x(C)\) simultaneously for every observed \(x\).

For \(j\in J_x(C)=\widehat J_x\), both denominators have magnitude at least \(a\), while unit normalization bounds \(|C_{yj}|\le1\). Using (19) coordinatewise gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\widehat C_{yj}}{\widehat C_{xj}}-\frac{C_{yj}}{C_{xj}}\right|
 \le \frac{|\widehat C_{yj}-C_{yj}|}{|\widehat C_{xj}|}
 +\frac{|C_{yj}|\,|\widehat C_{xj}-C_{xj}|}{|\widehat C_{xj}|\,|C_{xj}|}
 \le(a^{-1}+a^{-2})b_N=w_N. \tag{20}
\]
Thus every true ratio belongs to its interval in \(\mathcal U_{xy}\). Conversely, every point of that interval is within \(w_N\) of its estimated center and, by (20), within another \(w_N\) of the corresponding true ratio. Hence
\[
 \mathcal R_{xy}(C)\subseteq\mathcal U_{xy},
 \qquad
 d_H(\mathcal U_{xy},\mathcal R_{xy}(C))\le2w_N \tag{21}
\]
simultaneously for all \(x\ne y\). If either deterministic informative-regime inequality fails, the definition gives \(\mathcal U_{xy}=[-a^{-1},a^{-1}]\); every admissible ratio lies in this interval because its numerator is at most one and its denominator is at least \(a\). Coverage therefore holds in both regimes on the single event \(E_N\), and (15) proves the displayed uniform probability bound. Finally, with dimensions, margins, \(M\), and \(\alpha\) fixed, \(L_m\), \(L_C\), and \(H\) are constants, so \(\tau_N=O(N^{-1/2})\) and \(2w_N=O(N^{-1/2})\).

statements.statement: For a fixed normalized representation \(X=C\varepsilon\) with mutually independent, nondegenerate, moment-determinate non-Gaussian sources and pairwise nonproportional mixing columns, set \(m_{\mathrm V}=n-1\) and \(R_0=3m_{\mathrm V}\). There is an exact population inverse which, for each cumulant order \(\nu\ge R_0\), reshapes \(\operatorname{cum}_\nu(X)\) with block degrees at least \(m_{\mathrm V}\), takes its unique minimal three-factor decomposition, and unions the recovered projective directions. It stops after a finite representation-dependent order and recovers \(\{[c_1],\ldots,[c_n]\}\), hence every \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\), without cross-order label alignment. No finite stopping order is uniform over the stated moment-determinate class. Already for \(p=n=2\), that class admits two fixed, separated direction sets and associated sequences of observational experiments whose \(N\)-sample total-variation distance tends to zero. Consequently no inverse is uniformly consistent there, and no confidence procedure with coverage strictly greater than one half can have uniformly vanishing Hausdorff uncertainty, so a uniform root-\(N\) heterogeneous-order frontier law does not follow without quantitative non-Gaussianity, moment, Veronese-conditioning, angular, probe/eigen-gap, deletion-rank, and denominator margins. The existing common-order separated theorem retains its simultaneous coverage and root-\(N\) conclusion.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\lambda_{j,\nu}=\operatorname{cum}_\nu(\varepsilon_j)\). Mutual independence implies additivity of the log characteristic function:
\[
 \log\mathbb E\exp(i t^{\top}X)
 =\sum_{j=1}^n\log\mathbb E\exp\{i(t^{\top}c_j)\varepsilon_j\}.
\]
Equating the formal derivatives of total order \(\nu\), which exist because the moment sequences exist, gives the observable cumulant tensor
\[
 \mathcal T_\nu=\operatorname{cum}_\nu(X)
 =\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_{j,\nu}c_j^{\otimes \nu}. \tag{23}
\]
Set \(m_{\mathrm V}=n-1\). For \(\nu\ge R_0=3m_{\mathrm V}\), take \(\ell_1=\ell_2=m_{\mathrm V}\) and \(\ell_3=\nu-2m_{\mathrm V}\), so \(\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\ge m_{\mathrm V}\). Let \(A_\nu=\{j:\lambda_{j,\nu}\ne0\}\) and \(R_\nu=|A_\nu|\). Reshaping (23) into three blocks yields
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_\nu
 =\sum_{j\in A_\nu}\lambda_{j,\nu}
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes \ell_1})\otimes
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes \ell_2})\otimes
 \operatorname{vec}(c_j^{\otimes \ell_3}). \tag{24}
\]
If \(R_\nu=0\), the tensor is zero and contributes no direction. If \(R_\nu\ge1\), the Veronese--Lagrange lemma applies because each block degree is at least \(n-1\ge R_\nu-1\). Thus each of the three factor matrices in (24) has Kruskal rank \(R_\nu\). For \(R_\nu\ge2\),
\[
 k_{\ell_1}+k_{\ell_2}+k_{\ell_3}=3R_\nu\ge2R_\nu+2,
\]
so Kruskal's cited Theorem 4a makes (24) essentially unique, up to one common permutation and reciprocal component scalings. The case \(R_\nu=1\) is immediate. The decomposition has minimal rank \(R_\nu\): its mode-one matricization has rank \(R_\nu\), since the first factor matrix has full column rank and the Khatri--Rao product of the other two factor matrices has full column rank. For the latter assertion, applying a left-inverse row for one column of the second factor matrix to a putative linear dependence isolates a nonzero third-factor column and forces that coefficient to vanish.

This gives an explicit population recovery operation at order \(\nu\): minimize \(R\) over integers \(0\le R\le n\) and variables \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_R\ne0\) and nonzero block factors \(z_{s\ell}\), subject to
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal T}_\nu=\sum_{\ell=1}^R\gamma_\ell z_{1\ell}\otimes z_{2\ell}\otimes z_{3\ell},
 \qquad z_{1\ell}\in\{\operatorname{vec}(z^{\otimes \ell_1}):z\ne0\},
\]
with the analogous Veronese constraints of degrees \(\ell_2\) and \(\ell_3\) on \(z_{2\ell}\) and \(z_{3\ell}\), and with the three factors in each summand required to have a common projective preimage. The preceding rank and uniqueness argument proves that its solution set is exactly the active directions in (24), modulo permutation and component scalings. The Veronese map is injective on real projective space: if \(z^{\otimes \ell_1}\) and \(w^{\otimes \ell_1}\) are proportional while \(z,w\) are not, a linear functional vanishing at \(w\) but not at \(z\), contracted in all \(\ell_1\) modes, gives a contradiction. Hence every active \([c_j]\) is computable from the exact tensor.

By the cited Marcinkiewicz cumulant theorem, every nondegenerate non-Gaussian source with moments of all orders has infinitely many nonzero cumulants. Therefore, for each \(j\), some \(\nu_j\ge R_0\) has \(\lambda_{j,\nu_j}\ne0\). Since there are only \(n\) sources,
\[
 K_{C,\varepsilon}=\max_{1\le j\le n}\nu_j<\infty. \tag{25}
\]
Incrementing \(\nu\) from \(R_0\), decomposing (24), and taking the set-theoretic union of the recovered projective directions stops as soon as the union has its known size \(n\), no later than (25). Pairwise nonproportionality prevents accidental merging. No labels need be transported between orders. Column ratios and deletion ranks are invariant under nonzero rescaling and permutation, so applying the deletion-rank map to these projective directions recovers every \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\).

We next prove that the stopping order and inference conclusion cannot be uniform under the frozen qualitative assumptions. Fix any finite \(K\ge3\). The near-Gaussian moment-matching lemma supplies a non-Gaussian moment-determinate law \(F\) whose first \(K\) moments equal those of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\). Let two independent sources have law \(F\), and consider
\[
 C_0=I_2,
 \qquad
 C_1=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\gamma&-\sin\gamma\\[2pt]\sin\gamma&\cos\gamma\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad 0<\gamma<\pi/4. \tag{26}
\]
Both matrices have normalized, nonzero, nonproportional columns. Independence and equality of the univariate moments through \(K\) imply that all joint source moments through total degree \(K\) are Gaussian. Orthogonal invariance of the Gaussian moments then shows that the two observed models in (26) have identical moments, and hence identical cumulant tensors, through order \(K\), although their projective direction sets are separated by angle \(\gamma\). No inverse using a uniformly fixed finite order can distinguish them.

For the statistical obstruction, use the same bounded perturbation construction with laws \(F_t\) satisfying \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F_t,\mathcal N(0,1))\to0\). Let \(P_{0,t}\) and \(P_{1,t}\) be the observed laws under the two matrices in (26). Total variation contracts under measurable maps and obeys the product bound, while both orthogonal images of two independent standard Gaussians equal \(\mathcal N(0,I_2)\). Hence
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_{0,t},P_{1,t})
 \le4d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F_t,\mathcal N(0,1)). \tag{27}
\]
Choose \(t=t_N\) so that the right side is at most \(N^{-2}\). The product inequality gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_{0,t_N}^{\otimes N},P_{1,t_N}^{\otimes N})\le N^{-1}\longrightarrow0. \tag{28}
\]
The two direction sets in (26) remain a fixed positive projective distance apart. If a direction estimator were uniformly consistent, choosing the nearer of those two fixed sets would define a test whose sum of error probabilities tends to zero. For every test region \(A\), however,
\[
 P_{0,t_N}^{\otimes N}(A^c)+P_{1,t_N}^{\otimes N}(A)
 \ge1-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_{0,t_N}^{\otimes N},P_{1,t_N}^{\otimes N}),
\]
which tends to one by (28), a contradiction.

The causal frontiers are separated as well. For \(x=1,y=2\), direct evaluation of the deletion minors gives
\[
 \mathcal R_{12}(C_0)=\{0\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal R_{12}(C_1)=\{\tan\gamma,-\cot\gamma\}. \tag{29}
\]
Thus the same testing argument rules out uniform Hausdorff consistency for the frontier. More generally, suppose a random confidence region for the frontier has uniform coverage \(1-\alpha>1/2\) and uniformly vanishing Hausdorff diameter. By (28), under the first experiment it contains the first frontier with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) and the second with probability at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\). Their intersection has probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)>0\), but on that intersection its diameter is at least the fixed Hausdorff separation in (29), a contradiction.

Two deterministic boundary sequences show why the causal map additionally needs denominator and deletion-rank margins. After harmless column normalization, for
\[
 D_t=\begin{pmatrix}t&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad t\to0,
\]
the frontier \(\mathcal R_{12}(D_t)=\{1/t,1\}\) for \(t\ne0,1\), whereas \(\mathcal R_{12}(D_0)=\{1\}\). For
\[
 E_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0&1\\1&0&0&0\\0&0&1&1\end{pmatrix}
\]
and \(E_t\) obtained by replacing its \((2,2)\) entry by \(t\ne0\), one checks \(\mathcal R_{12}(E_0)=\{0\}\) but \(\mathcal R_{12}(E_t)=\{0,t,1\}\). All columns are nonzero and pairwise nonproportional near zero, and the matrices have full row rank. Thus qualitative nonvanishing and rank conditions alone do not yield a uniform modulus. Quantitative lower cumulant, moment, Veronese-conditioning, angular, probe/eigen-gap, deletion-rank, and denominator controls are precisely the type of hypotheses needed for a robust finite-order analysis; the frozen common-order separated class supplies them, and the already proved common-order inverse and confidence theorem retain their simultaneous coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff conclusion. The heterogeneous population inverse is therefore positive, while heterogeneous uniform inference over the unrestricted class is negative rather than solved.

statements.statement: Let \(R\ge1\), let \(z_1,\ldots,z_R\) be nonzero pairwise nonproportional vectors in a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let \(s\ge R-1\). Then the columns \(z_1^{\otimes s},\ldots,z_R^{\otimes s}\) have Kruskal rank \(R\); equivalently, every subcollection is linearly independent.
statements.proof_tex:
It suffices to prove independence for an arbitrary subcollection \(z_1,\ldots,z_k\), where \(1\le k\le R\). For each ordered pair \(i
e j\), nonproportionality supplies a linear functional \(\ell_{ij}\) such that \(\ell_{ij}(z_j)=0\) and \(\ell_{ij}(z_i)
e0\): take a functional vanishing on the line spanned by \(z_j\) but not on \(z_i\). Choose also a linear functional \(g_i\) with \(g_i(z_i)
e0\). The homogeneous polynomial
\[
 f_i(z)=g_i(z)^{s-k+1}\prod_{j
e i}\ell_{ij}(z)
\]
has degree \(s\), is nonzero at \(z_i\), and vanishes at every \(z_j\) with \(j
e i\). Every homogeneous polynomial of degree \(s\) is a linear functional on the symmetric tensor power, so there is \(L_i\) with \(L_i(z^{\otimes s})=f_i(z)\). If \(\sum_{j=1}^k a_jz_j^{\otimes s}=0\), applying \(L_i\) gives \(a_if_i(z_i)=0\), hence \(a_i=0\). This holds for every \(i\), proving independence of the arbitrary subcollection and therefore Kruskal rank \(R\).

statements.statement: For every integer \(K\ge3\) and every \(\rho>0\), there exists a centered, variance-one, non-Gaussian, moment-determinate probability law \(F\) on \(\mathbb R\) such that \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F,\mathcal N(0,1))<\rho\) and the first \(K\) raw moments, hence the cumulants through order \(K\), agree with those of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(\phi\) be the standard Gaussian density. Choose \(K+2\) pairwise disjoint bounded intervals \(I_0,\ldots,I_{K+1}\), each of positive Gaussian probability. The \((K+1)\)-by-\((K+2)\) matrix
\[
 A_{r\ell}=\int_{I_\ell}x^r\phi(x)\,dx,
 \qquad 0\le r\le K,
\]
has a nonzero null vector \(b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{K+1})\). Rescale it so that \(\max_\ell|b_\ell|=1\), and define the bounded, nonzero function \(h=\sum_\ell b_\ell\mathbf 1_{I_\ell}\). Then
\[
 \int x^rh(x)\phi(x)\,dx=0,
 \qquad 0\le r\le K. \tag{22}
\]
For \(0<t<1\), set \(f_t(x)=\phi(x)(1+th(x))\). The case \(r=0\) of (22) makes \(f_t\) integrate to one, and \(|h|\le1\) makes it strictly positive. Since \(h\) is nonzero on a set of positive Gaussian measure, \(f_t\ne\phi\). Equation (22) says that its first \(K\) moments, including mean zero and variance one, equal the Gaussian moments. Cumulants through order \(K\) are universal polynomials in the moments through the same order, so they also agree.

Moreover \(f_t\le2\phi\), whence its even moments satisfy \(m_{2s}(f_t)\le2(2s-1)!!\). It follows that \(m_{2s}(f_t)^{-1/(2s)}\) is bounded below by a positive constant times \(s^{-1/2}\), and therefore the Carleman series diverges. The cited Carleman criterion makes \(F_t\) moment determinate. Finally,
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(F_t,\mathcal N(0,1))
 =\frac t2\int|h(x)|\phi(x)\,dx\longrightarrow0
\]
as \(t\downarrow0\). Choosing \(t\) small enough proves the claim.

statements.statement:
Let \(C\varepsilon\) and \(A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\xi^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\) be two irreducible independent-component representations of the same \(p\)-dimensional law, where irreducible means that the mixing matrix has neither zero columns nor proportional column pairs. If \(C\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\in\mathbb R^{p\times m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}}\), the source coordinates are mutually independent and nondegenerate, and every coordinate of \(\varepsilon\) is non-Gaussian, then \(m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=n\), every column of one mixing matrix is proportional to a unique column of the other, and every coordinate of \(\xi^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\) is non-Gaussian. Equivalently, there are a permutation matrix \(\Pi\) and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D\) such that
\[
 A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=C\Pi D.
\]

statements.statement:
For every \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\), the response vector is well defined and
\[
 \rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M})
 =\left(
 \frac{((Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}})^{-1})_{ix}}
 {((Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}})^{-1})_{xx}}
 \right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(Q=Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\), \(H=H^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\), and \(\xi=\xi^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\). Membership in the law fiber gives \(\det(Q)\ne0\) and \(\det(Q_{-x,-x})\ne0\). The diagonal cofactor formula therefore gives
\[
 (Q^{-1})_{xx}=\frac{\det(Q_{-x,-x})}{\det(Q)}\ne0. \tag{1}
\]
After the perfect intervention replaces the \(x\)-th equation by \(V_x=t\), the remaining equations are
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}V_{-x}=H_{-x,:}\xi-Q_{-x,x}t. \tag{2}
\]
The postintervention determinant condition makes (2) uniquely solvable, and differentiation with the disturbances held fixed yields
\[
 \frac{\partial V_{-x}}{\partial t}=-Q_{-x,-x}^{-1}Q_{-x,x}. \tag{3}
\]
On the other hand, the rows different from \(x\) in \(QQ^{-1}e_x=e_x\) give
\[
 Q_{-x,-x}(Q^{-1})_{-x,x}+Q_{-x,x}(Q^{-1})_{xx}=0. \tag{4}
\]
Multiplying (4) by \(Q_{-x,-x}^{-1}\) and dividing by the nonzero quantity in (1) shows that the right-hand side of (3) equals \((Q^{-1})_{-x,x}/(Q^{-1})_{xx}\). Restricting to the observed coordinates different from \(x\) and invoking the definition of \(\rho_x\) proves the claim.

statements.statement:
Let \(C'=C\Pi D\), where \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\) is a permutation matrix and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) has \(d_k\ne0\) for every \(k\). Then
\[
 k\in J_x(C')\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi(k)\in J_x(C),
\]
and consequently \(\mathcal V_x(C')=\mathcal V_x(C)\) and \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C')=\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\).

Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\) and suppose \(m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=n\) and \(A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=C\Pi D\), where \(\Pi e_k=e_{\pi(k)}\) and \(D\) is nonsingular diagonal. Define
\[
 H^C=H^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}D^{-1}\Pi^\top,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M^C=(Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}},H^C).
\]
Then \(\mathcal M^C\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\). For every \(i\in\mathsf O\), if \(s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}^{\mathrm{law}}(i)=k\), then \(s_{\mathcal M^C}(i)=\pi(k)=\bar s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(i)\). The inverse structural matrix, its intervention minor, and every equilibrium response ratio are unchanged by this canonicalization.

For every \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\), one has \(m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=n\), the aligned source \(j=\bar s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(x)\) belongs to \(J_x(C)\), and
\[
 \rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M})
 =\left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}
 \in\mathcal V_x(C).
\]
In particular, \(C_{xj}\ne0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(C_{-x,-j})=p-1\).
statements.proof_tex:
The reference representation \((C,\varepsilon)\) is irreducible because its columns are nonzero and pairwise nonproportional. Its sources are mutually independent, nondegenerate, and non-Gaussian by the corresponding population assumptions. The representation \((A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}},\xi^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}})\) is irreducible by the law-fiber definition, and it has the same observed law. The cited irreducible-OICA uniqueness lemma therefore gives
\[
 m_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=n,
 \qquad
 A^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}=C\Pi D \tag{9}
\]
for a permutation matrix \(\Pi\) and a nonsingular diagonal matrix \(D\).

Apply the monomial-canonicalization lemma to (9). It returns \(\mathcal M^C\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\) whose source assigned to equation \(x\) is
\[
 s_{\mathcal M^C}(x)=\bar s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(x)=j. \tag{10}
\]
The established necessary deletion-rank lemma applied to \(\mathcal M^C\) yields \(j\in J_x(C)\); expanding the definition of \(J_x(C)\) gives the final two asserted conditions.

It remains to identify the whole vector. The established intervention-ratio lemma is stated for an arbitrary observed outcome distinct from \(x\), so instantiate it at each \(i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\). For the fixed-fiber completion \(\mathcal M^C\) it gives
\[
 \frac{((Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}})^{-1})_{ix}}
 {((Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}})^{-1})_{xx}}
 =\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}, \tag{11}
\]
because canonicalization leaves \(Q^{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}\) unchanged. Combining (11) with the hard-intervention response formula proves the displayed vector equality. Its membership in \(\mathcal V_x(C)\) is then exactly the response-frontier definition.

statements.statement:
For every \(j\in J_x(C)\), let \(\mathcal M_j=(Q_j,H_j)\) be the fixed-law completion returned by \(\operatorname{Cert}(C,x)\), and set
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal M}_j=(n,Q_j,H_j,\varepsilon).
\]
Then \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j\in\mathfrak F_x^{\mathrm{law}}(P_X)\), \(\bar s_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j}(x)=j\), and
\[
 \rho_x(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_j)
 =\left(\frac{C_{ij}}{C_{xj}}\right)_{i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}}.
\]
If \(C\) is rational, \(Q_j\) and \(H_j\) are rational.
statements.proof_tex:
The established shear-and-matching sufficiency lemma gives \(\mathcal M_j=(Q_j,H_j)\in\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\), assigns source \(j\) to equation \(x\), and gives rational \(Q_j,H_j\) when \(C\) is rational. By the fixed-law match,
\[
 \bigl[Q_j^{-1}H_j\bigr]_{\mathsf O,:}=C. \tag{12}
\]
Consequently the embedded model has observed law
\[
 \mathcal L\bigl([Q_j^{-1}H_j]_{\mathsf O,:}\varepsilon\bigr)
 =\mathcal L(C\varepsilon)=P_X. \tag{13}
\]
All diagonal, monomial, observational-solvability, and postintervention-solvability conditions are inherited from fixed-fiber membership. The source conditions follow from the independent, nondegenerate, non-Gaussian reference-source assumptions. Equation (12) and the nonzero, pairwise nonproportional column assumptions make the embedded representation irreducible. Thus every condition in the law-fiber definition holds.

Since its observed mixing matrix is exactly \(C\), the source direction assigned to equation \(x\) aligns with the same index \(j\); distinct directions make that index unique. Finally, instantiate the established intervention-ratio lemma at every \(i\in\mathsf O\setminus\{x\}\), and combine it with the hard-intervention response formula. This gives the displayed vector equality. The rationality conclusion is precisely the rationality conclusion of the established sufficiency lemma.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 4 constructs square candidates by admissible row permutation and row normalization, while Theorem 1 states distribution-entailment equivalence of the LiNG-D output; it does not assert solvability after a specified intervention.
The main equivalence theorem characterizes equality of graph-indexed observed distribution families by children-basis and perfect-matching conditions.
The total-effect theorem gives a complete graphical criterion for generic effect identification in acyclic latent-variable LiNGAM.
The cyclic section gives a necessary coefficient-identification condition in general and a complete result for restricted cycle structures.
The main theorem gives an if-and-only-if population identifiability criterion for overcomplete ICA and an associated coupled recovery method.
Theorem 4a gives essential uniqueness of a three-factor tensor decomposition under the Kruskal-rank inequality.
The paper develops robust tensor-decomposition methods under quantitative nondegeneracy conditions.
The finite-cumulant-sequence theorem implies that a nondegenerate non-Gaussian law with all moments has infinitely many nonzero higher cumulants.

tldr: A fixed normalized overcomplete-ICA law can support many source-minimal cyclic latent structural completions, yet its ordered equilibrium effect has an exact finite image. The image is the set of source-column ratios whose complementary deletion matrix has full row rank. Necessity follows from intervention solvability; constructive sufficiency uses one latent-row shear and one perfect matching, producing exact same-law countermodels and an \(O(n^4)\) all-witness algorithm. On a separated common-cumulant-order iid class, an explicit tensor-pencil inverse yields simultaneous coverage and root-\(N\) Hausdorff uncertainty for the finite frontier. Heterogeneous source-specific cumulant orders remain a first-class open problem.

project_justification.gap: Published latent cyclic LiNG work characterizes graph-level distributional equivalence or coefficients in a known mixed graph, while published latent acyclic work gives graphical effect criteria. None of these results characterizes the numerical intervention-effect image of every source-minimal cyclic completion of one fixed overcomplete-ICA representation.
project_justification.niche: The fixed-law fiber supplies numerical source directions, so a query-specific algebraic criterion can be both sharper and much smaller than the compatible graph class without imposing dynamical stability.
project_justification.fill: The deletion-rank frontier gives necessary and sufficient attainability, exact witnesses, point-identification and countermodel certificates, polynomial-time enumeration, and a separated iid inference layer with explicit finite-sample coverage.

related_work: DaiAlbrechtSpirtesZhang2026 provides the writing and identification exemplar: its introduction moves from latent cyclic ambiguity to equivalence-class structure, and its main proof converts children bases into perfect matchings; the present target instead fixes one numerical law and projects its completion fiber onto one equilibrium effect. TramontanoKivvaSalehkaleybarDrtonKiyavash2024 motivates query-specific effect identification and proves complete acyclic criteria, while its conclusion leaves cyclic extensions open. TramontanoDrtonEtesami2026 studies coefficient identification for a known mixed graph and obtains only partial cyclic criteria, a different conditioning object from the fixed source-direction fiber. In LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008, Section 4 constructs square candidates by admissible row permutations, while Theorem 1 states that LiNG-D returns a distribution-entailment equivalence class. The equality of the candidates' equilibrium-effect projection with \(\mathcal R_{xy}(C)\) is the new square-case reduction here. BongersForrePetersMooij2021 supplies the distinction between observational and interventional solvability. WangSeigal2026 supplies the OICA identification and coupled-decomposition benchmark, AnandkumarGeJanzamin2015 supplies the tensor perturbation technique, and ChenBickel2006 supplies the asymptotic ICA motivation; none studies a rank-selected causal set. PodosinnikovaEtAl2019 and VirtaNordhausenOja2016 inform the heterogeneous-order open question. NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 confirms that joint interventions require globally compatible assignments rather than Cartesian products, motivating but not subsuming the deferred joint-frontier seed.
technical_internal_limitation: Source minimality means exactly one distinct disturbance per structural equation, with no source sharing or splitting, and the fixed-law convention holds one recovered normalized OICA representation fixed while latent rows vary. Enlarging the fiber to split or duplicated sources, graphically irreducible completions, or alternate normalized source representations can change the frontier, so no invariance claim is made for those larger objects. The rank and denominator margins exclude the discontinuity surfaces on which uniform root-\(N\) Hausdorff inference is impossible. The fourteen-stock Hong Kong series is a consumer of the population certificate only: its serial dependence and documented mechanism changes violate the iid inference model unless a separate dependent-time-series theorem and an empirical separation certificate are supplied.
honest_scope: The theorem spine asks for the scalar fixed-law frontier, constructive sharpness, exact countermodels, and iid inference on a nonempty common-order separated class with \(d\ge1\), \(q\ge1\), and \(n\le\binom{p+d-1}{d}\). In the square case, LacerdaSpirtesRamseyHoyer2008 Section 4 supplies admissible row-permutation candidates and its Theorem 1 supplies the distribution-entailment statement; equality of their effect projection with the deletion-rank frontier is the reduction claimed here. Stability-refined completions, common-completion joint intervention matrices, dependent-time-series inference for the Hong Kong data, representation invariance beyond a fixed normalized OICA tuple, and source-specific multi-order recovery are not claimed. The last item is retained as the explicit open-ended question with a concrete coupled-Hessian and multi-cumulant handle.
